explain.say: The Earth spins once a day, so you might expect the Moon to rise at the same time every day. But while Earth spins, the Moon is also moving eastward along its orbit.

explain.say: Each day the Moon moves about 13 degrees along its orbit. Earth has to turn for about 50 extra minutes to catch up with it, so moonrise comes about 50 minutes later each day.

explain.say: Over a month those delays add up. A new moon rises with the Sun at dawn, a first quarter moon around midday, and a full moon around sunset, opposite the Sun.

explain.say: A last quarter moon rises around midnight, so it is best seen in the morning sky. That's why you can often see the Moon in daytime: for much of the month it is up while the Sun is too.

faq.q: Why does the Moon rise later each day?
faq.a: The Moon travels eastward around Earth, about 13 degrees a day. After one spin of the Earth, the Moon has moved on, so Earth needs about 50 more minutes to bring it back over the horizon.
asks: Why is moonrise later every night?

faq.q: When does a full moon rise?
faq.a: Around sunset. A full moon is opposite the Sun in the sky, so it rises in the east as the Sun sets in the west, and is up all night.
asks: Why is the full moon up all night?

faq.q: Why can you see the Moon in the daytime?
faq.a: The Moon is above the horizon for about 12 hours a day, but those hours shift through the month. For much of the month, part of that time is daytime, and the Moon is bright enough to see in a blue sky.
asks: Why is the Moon out during the day?

faq.q: When does a new moon rise?
faq.a: With the Sun, around dawn, because it is in nearly the same direction. It crosses the sky with the Sun and is lost in its glare, so we can't see it.
asks: Where is the new moon in the sky?

faq.q: Is it always exactly 50 minutes later?
faq.a: No, 50 minutes is the average. The delay can range from under half an hour to more than an hour, depending on the season and your latitude. Around the September equinox, the Harvest Moon rises only a little later on each night.

facts: On average the Moon rises about 50 minutes later each day.
The Moon moves about 13 degrees eastward against the stars each day.
A full moon rises around sunset and sets around sunrise.

quiz.say: At what time of day does a full moon rise?
quiz.why: A full moon is opposite the Sun, so it comes up in the east just as the Sun goes down in the west.

wrong.0: Around noon it is the first quarter moon that rises.
wrong.1: Around sunrise it is the new moon that rises, together with the Sun.
